sentences.text: The species name mephistocephalus describes its distinctive devilish squamosal horns.
A large articulated skeleton was found in 1996 by a Belgian-Chinese expedition in the Bayan Mandahu Formation of China.
Pascal Godefroit and colleagues originally named this specimen IMM 96BM3/1 as Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus in 1999.
Paul Penkalski later transferred this species to the new genus Eopinacosaurus in 2026.
Eopinacosaurus is classified as a member of the ankylosaurid subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
It belongs to the class Ornithischia, family Ankylosauridae, and subfamily Ankylosaurinae.
The genus contains only a single species, Eopinacosaurus mephistocephalus.
Fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous Bayan Mandahu Formation of China and the Djadokhta Formation of Mongolia.
This animal lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
Gregory S. Paul suggested in 2010 that Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus was a junior synonym of Pinacosaurus grangeri.
Phylogenetic analyses have recovered Eopinacosaurus in a variable position within the clade relative to the type species of Pinacosaurus.
